title.narrative: Gwanda Readiness and Anticipatory Action Project (GRAAP)-Phase 2 Action

description.narrative: The GRAAP project aims is planned for November to January 2026, funded by STARTNETWORK Start Ready Risk Pool 4, implemented through Lutheran Development Services in Gwanda district of Zimbabwe, to enhance preparedness for 2,000 at-risk households (potentially benefiting 8,000 individuals) in four vulnerable wards (16, 19- new; 17 and 24-old) of Gwanda to reduce impending drought impact. A rapid AA assessment conducted in 2024 highlighted significant concerns related to food and water security due to a poor agricultural season marked by inadequate rainfall and prolonged dry spells, which adversely affect food crops, pasture development, and water recharge. As the peak drought period approaches, the project anticipates increased water scarcity for both domestic use and livestock, leading to a rise in diseases. The project will strengthen civil protection mechanisms at both the district and ward levels, enhancing DRR capabilities. It will also improve access to water resources through the expansion of high-yielding boreholes for human and agricultural use. Furthermore, the project will preposition agricultural inputs, including drought-tolerant food crops and pasture seeds. The project will enhance timely access to information on seasonal preparedness, drought conditions, food security, and water availability via local radio in languages using the Participatory Integrated Climate Service for Agriculture (PISCA) to enhance understanding of climate information and making informed decisions about best agricultural practices. Additionally, PSEAH in the anticipatory action project will be considered to protect vulnerable populations, build community trust, and empower individuals to speak out against abuse during crises.
